# Pi advisor: isolated consultation contract and design

## Purpose and scope {#scope}

Pi advisor gives the main agent a separate reasoning partner. The main agent explains the problem and supplies evidence across multiple turns.

The advisor cannot inspect code, run tools, or inherit the parent conversation. The main agent owns investigation, verification, implementation, and authorization.

The user requested a standalone extension, with a specification before implementation. This draft records the initial implementation contract, not separate policy approval.

V1 excludes persistence, restoration, automatic summarization, forks, autonomous consultation loops, workspace collection, custom providers, and a dependency on pi-magic8ball.

## Design and implementation choices {#design}

Use one process-local consultation manager per extension instance. Call the host model registry directly with an explicit tool-free context. Do not create a nested Pi agent runtime.

Consultations remain available across parent turns and compaction. Clear them on session start, tree navigation, and shutdown. Switch, fork, and reload replace the runtime. Do not restore consultations from tool results.

The extension writes no consultation files. Pi can still persist tool arguments and results in its parent transcript. The configured provider receives explicit consultation messages. Ephemeral means no separate extension persistence, not guaranteed erasure by Pi or the provider.

Initial resource defaults are implementation choices: 8 simultaneous consultations, 24 successful exchange pairs, 16384 UTF-8 bytes per input or reply, and 49152 transcript bytes. Each request has a 120000 ms deadline and requests at most 4096 output tokens. These bounds are not token-context or monetary guarantees.

Settings use the host agent directory, not a hard-coded home path. Project settings require current Pi project trust. No default model is selected. No live provider calls are part of build verification.

## Tool and lifecycle contract {#contract}

<a id="REQ-1"></a>

**REQ-1** Isolated multi-turn consultation

The extension MUST expose advisor({message, session?}). Omitted session starts a new consultation. Present session continues only that consultation.
Message MUST be a nonblank string. Session MUST be a nonempty opaque identifier when present. Null and unknown fields MUST fail validation.
On successful creation, the extension MUST pin the explicitly configured physical chat model. Continuations MUST use that selection despite later configuration changes.
Every model request MUST contain only the fixed advisor system prompt and that consultation's explicit exchanges. It MUST declare zero tools.
The extension MUST NOT read parent messages, instructions, source files, environment model selections, or another consultation's exchanges into the request.


<a id="REQ-2"></a>

**REQ-2** Advice and output protocol

The advisor prompt MUST distinguish reported observations, interpretations, assumptions, and hypotheses. It MUST permit questions and challenges to the main agent's framing.
The prompt MUST state that advice is not evidence or authorization. It MUST ask the main agent to gather missing evidence.
A valid reply MUST contain nonblank text followed by exactly one standalone final marker: [CONTINUE], [ACTIONABLE], [APPROVAL_NEEDED], or [EXHAUSTED].
These markers map to continue, actionable, approval_needed, and exhausted. The extension MUST remove the marker from response text.
Missing, repeated, misplaced, or unknown markers MUST produce invalid-response. Tool calls, nontext/nonthinking blocks, and non-stop completion reasons MUST fail.
Thinking content MUST NOT enter the returned response or retained transcript. Status MUST NOT close the consultation or grant permission to act.


<a id="REQ-3"></a>

**REQ-3** Atomic exchanges and failures

Each advisor call MUST make at most one model request. Provider retries MUST be disabled. Automatic fallback MUST NOT occur.
Only a validated reply MUST commit its user/reply pair. Failed creation MUST leave no consultation. Failed continuation MUST preserve previous exchanges.
The extension MUST combine caller cancellation with a 120000 ms deadline, measured from call entry. Cancellation MUST prevent a later commit.
Timeout and cancellation MUST return without waiting indefinitely for a provider that ignores abort. Late completions MUST NOT change state.
Concurrent calls on one consultation MUST reject the second with busy. Different consultations MAY run concurrently within the session limit.
Failures MUST use fixed safe error codes and messages. Raw provider exceptions MUST NOT appear in output.
Results MUST report usage available at return, including rejected completed replies. Usage from a late unobserved completion MAY be unavailable.


<a id="REQ-4"></a>

**REQ-4** Resource limits

The extension MUST enforce inclusive hard limits: 8 active consultations, 24 committed exchange pairs per consultation, and 16384 UTF-8 bytes per message or raw reply text.
Retained transcript bytes MUST equal the UTF-8 size of JSON.stringify([{role,text}, ...]) and MUST NOT exceed 49152 bytes.
The pending user entry MUST pass byte validation before model work. The full pair MUST pass validation before commit.
A request MUST specify maxTokens = 4096. Token limits remain subject to provider support. Byte and turn limits MUST hold locally.
Crossing a limit MUST return limit-exceeded without changing the prior transcript. The extension MUST NOT evict, trim, compact, or summarize implicitly.
Closed consultations MUST release their slot. Limits reset for a new consultation or a cleared parent lifecycle.


<a id="REQ-5"></a>

**REQ-5** Discovery, close, and reset

advisor_sessions({}) MUST return active consultation metadata only: session, label, turns, status, model, and busy.
Label MUST derive from the first explicit message, collapse whitespace, and contain at most 80 Unicode code points. No full transcript MUST appear.
advisor_close({session}) MUST remove an idle consultation and return its identifier. Unknown identifiers MUST return not-found. Busy close MUST return busy.
A cleared manager MUST abort all pending work and reject late commits. Old identifiers MUST become not-found.
The extension MUST clear state on session_start, session_tree, and session_shutdown. Pi 1.0.4 replaces the runtime on session switch and fork through shutdown/start.
Reload MUST create fresh state. Parent compaction MUST NOT clear consultations. State MUST NOT be reconstructed from persisted entries.


## Configuration contract {#configuration}

<a id="REQ-6"></a>

**REQ-6** Explicit trusted settings

Settings MUST be strict JSON objects with only optional model: {provider, model}. Both identifiers MUST be nonblank strings without control characters or whitespace.
Missing files and {} MUST mean unconfigured. Malformed, oversized, null, or unknown-field settings MUST fail closed.
The extension MUST read <agent-dir>/advisor.json first. Only a trusted project MAY add <cwd>/.pi/advisor.json.
A project model MUST replace the entire global model pair. An empty project object MUST retain the global pair. Invalid global settings MUST fail even with a valid project override.
Reads MUST accept only bounded regular UTF-8 files, at most 16384 bytes. Immediate parent or target symlinks and special files MUST be rejected.
A new consultation MUST fail with not-configured or model-unavailable when selection or authentication is unavailable. Virtual models MUST be rejected.
Normal Pi authentication MUST serve model requests. The extension MUST NOT read credentials or change the parent's active model.


<a id="REQ-7"></a>

**REQ-7** User-only settings command

The extension MUST register /advisor [--global|--project] [show | model <provider> <model>]. Global MUST be the default scope.
In TUI mode, a bare command MUST use the inline searchable picker defined by REQ-10. Other UI modes MUST retain the standard selection dialog.
Without UI, it MUST emit settings and usage as a Pi custom message.
Every non-UI command report MUST use customType advisor-settings, display: true, and triggerTurn: false. No report MUST start a model turn.
show MUST display effective selection and source. Invalid commands or cancelled selection MUST write nothing and call no model.
An explicit pair MUST resolve to a physical chat model before save. Project saves MUST recheck trust.
Saves MUST touch only advisor.json and owned temporary or lock files. They MUST serialize participating writers and acquire an exclusive lock.
Replacement MUST be atomic through a same-directory temporary file. First creation MUST NOT replace a newly appeared file.
At the final comparison, changed bytes or lock contention MUST fail closed. No stale-lock reclamation MUST occur.
Cleanup MUST remove only owned temporary files and locks. A save error MUST warn that a save may have completed and require inspection before retry.


<a id="REQ-10"></a>

**REQ-10** Model picker matches /model

The TUI picker MUST copy the inline interface pattern used by pi-magic8ball and Pi 1.0.4 /model.
It MUST show at most 10 model rows and at most max(1, terminal.rows - 2) total rows. Every rendered line MUST fit its terminal width.
It MUST provide editable fuzzy search across provider, model identifier, and display name, using Pi fuzzyFilter ranking.
Every nonempty query edit MUST select the best match. Text keys, including j and k, MUST edit the input.
Arrow keys MUST wrap through filtered results. The effective configured advisor model MUST appear first before search with a current-selection marker.
When at least 10 total rows fit, the picker MUST show the selected display name and navigation hints.
An empty result set MUST show No matching models. Enter with no match MUST leave the picker open.
Escape and Ctrl+C MUST cancel without settings writes. Focus MUST propagate to the search input for cursor and IME placement.
Navigation and resize MUST keep the selected item visible. Truncation MUST NOT change the model identifier returned or saved.
Non-TUI UI clients MUST retain the existing provider/model selection labels and cancellation behavior.
The picker MUST use the current available physical model snapshot. It MUST NOT generate, change the conversation model, or refresh remote catalogs.


## Host integration and results {#integration}

<a id="REQ-8"></a>

**REQ-8** Structured tool results

The package MUST register exactly advisor, advisor_sessions, and advisor_close as model-only tools. Each MUST define strict input and output schemas.
Successful advisor results MUST carry ok, advisory: true, session, response, status, turns, model, per-call usage, and cumulative consultation usage.
Failure results MUST carry ok: false, error: {code,message}, and per-call usage. Existing session identifiers MUST accompany continuation failures.
Tool content, details, and structuredContent MUST agree. Failures MUST set isError. Host usage MUST contain only this call's usage, not cumulative usage.
The tool guidance MUST tell the main agent to explain objective, understanding, evidence, constraints, and uncertainty. It MUST prohibit citing advice as evidence or permission.
It MUST recommend continuation for the same issue and disclose provider charges. The extension MUST NOT automatically execute advice or continue consultations.


<a id="REQ-9"></a>

**REQ-9** Standalone package and verification

The package MUST load through Pi's resource loader without model work. Loading MUST NOT change profile settings or start background resources.
Runtime Pi and TypeBox packages MUST remain host-provided optional wildcard peers. pi-magic8ball MUST NOT be a dependency.
The package MUST provide repeatable Node test and TypeScript check commands. Acceptance tests MUST use injected mock responses and temporary configuration directories.
The README MUST describe loading, model setup, multi-turn use, close, limits, ephemeral state, transcript retention caveats, and advisory responsibility.
Paid provider checks MUST require separate authorization. Offline checks MUST NOT claim model reasoning quality or provider interoperability.


## Acceptance criteria {#acceptance}

Every criterion below describes changed behavior. No prior pi-advisor behavior exists to preserve.

<a id="AC-1"></a>

**AC-1**

Start two consultations, then continue the first after changing configured selection. PASS when each request contains only its own exchanges, zero tools, and the first pinned model.


<a id="AC-2"></a>

**AC-2**

Exercise all four markers, thinking plus text, missing/repeated/misplaced markers, tool calls, and incomplete completions. PASS when valid outputs map correctly and invalid outputs commit nothing.
Inspect both prompts and tool guidance for evidence and authorization distinctions.


<a id="AC-3"></a>

**AC-3**

Inject provider exceptions, completed error responses, caller abort, deadline expiration, ignored abort with late success, and overlapping continuation.
PASS when each failure returns its safe code, makes no automatic retry, preserves history, accounts for known usage, and prevents late commits.


<a id="AC-4"></a>

**AC-4**

Test limits at their inclusive boundary and one unit beyond. Use multibyte text for byte limits.
PASS when allowed inputs commit, forbidden inputs return limit-exceeded, state stays bounded, no implicit compaction occurs, and closing releases capacity.


<a id="AC-5"></a>

**AC-5**

List, close, duplicate-close, close during a request, and reset during a request. PASS when metadata excludes transcript, close rejects unknown/busy identifiers, and reset prevents late commits.
Fire each clearing host event and compaction. PASS when clearing invalidates identifiers and compaction retains them.


<a id="AC-6"></a>

**AC-6**

Use absent, valid, malformed, oversized, null, unknown-field, symlink, and special-file settings. Test trusted and untrusted projects.
PASS when precedence follows REQ-6, untrusted project bytes are never consumed, and invalid settings fail closed.
Through the tool boundary, test missing selection, missing authentication, absent model, and virtual model. PASS when no request occurs.


<a id="AC-7"></a>

**AC-7**

Exercise show, explicit global/project save, bare selection, cancellation, unavailable model, invalid command, lost trust, and competing locks.
PASS when only validated user requests save advisor.json, saves remain strict and atomic, and cancellation/errors trigger no model call or unrelated write.


<a id="AC-8"></a>

**AC-8**

Inspect registered tools and validate successful/failed results against their schemas. PASS when exactly three model-only tools exist and content/details/structuredContent agree.
PASS when per-call usage reaches the host once, cumulative usage appears separately, and argument schemas reject null or unknown fields.


<a id="AC-9"></a>

**AC-9**

Load the package with the installed Pi resource loader without credentials or provider calls. Run Node acceptance checks and TypeScript checking.
PASS when discovery reports one extension, three tools, one command, no loader errors, host-only runtime peers, and no sibling dependency.
Verify README coverage of the required usage and retention caveats.

<a id="AC-10"></a>

**AC-10**

Changed behavior: invoke /advisor in TUI mode with 100 available models and a configured advisor selection.
PASS when the actual command-selected component renders inline, selects and marks the current model, and shows at most 10 model rows.
Exercise provider/identifier/name fuzzy queries, input editing with j and k, clearing, arrow wrap, and an empty result set.
PASS when each query selects the Pi-ranked best match, no-match Enter stays open, and clearing restores results.
Render at heights 60, 24, 10, 6, 3, and 1 and widths 30 and 80. Repeat with long Unicode identifiers.
PASS when rows and widths fit, selection remains visible, and saved identifiers remain complete. Verify focus reaches the search input.
Cancel with Escape and Ctrl+C after navigation. PASS when global and project settings stay byte-identical and no model call occurs.
Preserved behavior: existing AC-1 through AC-9 checks MUST pass before and after this change. Non-TUI dialogs MUST keep their existing labels and persistence behavior.

## Verification scope {#verification}

The initial 12 acceptance checks failed against the minimal baseline. Failures identified missing consultation behavior, settings behavior, or registration.

All 12 checks then passed with implementation. TypeScript checking passed. A clean source copy also passed after npm ci --ignore-scripts --offline.

No preserved-behavior baseline applies. This package did not exist before the task.

| Criterion | Check names in tests/ | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AC-1 | isolated starts and continuations pin the selected model; tool boundary uses explicit context | fail | pass |
| AC-2 | reply protocol validates markers and does not expose thinking | fail | pass |
| AC-3 | atomic failures, usage, busy, abort, timeout and late completions | fail | pass |
| AC-4 | hard byte, pair, transcript, and session limits preserve state | fail | pass |
| AC-5 | metadata-only discovery, busy close, deletion and reset; clears on lifecycle, not compaction | fail | pass |
| AC-6 | strict settings precedence, trust, bounds, symlinks and special files; tool preflight rejects unavailable selection | fail | pass |
| AC-7 | atomic settings saves, validation, trust and exclusive locks; user-only configuration | fail | pass |
| AC-8 | registration, strict schemas, coherent results and usage | fail | pass |
| AC-9 | standalone loader discovers extension without provider work and README covers boundaries | fail | pass |

Additional failing-then-passing cases verified an extra unknown marker, a missing identifier on oversized continuation errors, and non-UI command reporting.

Commands run in the project: npm run verify and npm pack --dry-run --ignore-scripts. Package discovery used the complete package directory, not only the entry-point file.

The nine new-coder profile check scripts passed. Both documented profile core TypeScript commands passed.

These results cover deterministic boundaries and Pi 1.0.4 package loading on Node 24, on Linux. They do not establish reasoning quality or live provider interoperability.

No paid model request, live terminal session, hosted CI run, Windows check, or macOS check occurred. Provider-side retention remains outside this extension's control.

Settings safety is checkpoint-based. An external writer can race between the final byte comparison and replacement. Parent-directory races remain outside the guarantee.

No unresolved implementation decision blocks this initial version. Resource defaults and marker syntax remain revisable before a public release.

### Model picker correction {#model-picker-verification}

The user requested the /model interface and named pi-magic8ball as the reference.

REQ-10 and AC-10 replace the generic TUI selection dialog with the sibling extension's inline searchable interface.
The copied picker uses public Pi TUI components. It does not instantiate Pi's session-bound ModelSelectorComponent or refresh remote catalogs.

Preserved baseline: all 12 existing AC-1 through AC-9 checks passed before and after this change.
Changed behavior: all four AC-10 checks failed before implementation because the command used the generic dialog.
All four then passed. The complete suite now passes 16 checks. TypeScript checking also passes.

AC-10 check names in tests/model-picker.test.mjs:

- inline picker selects current model, caps rows, forwards focus and handles resize
- fuzzy search matches names and provider/model tokens with editable j/k
- no-match Enter stays open, clear restores results, arrows wrap and cancellation writes nothing
- Unicode truncation preserves complete saved identifiers

A clean source copy passed npm ci --ignore-scripts --offline and npm run verify.
The tests construct and exercise the actual command-selected component with mocked terminal dimensions.
These checks do not establish appearance in a live terminal. No paid model calls or profile settings changes occurred.

The picker preserves the prior provider/model labels for RPC and other non-TUI UI clients.
No additional requirement or unresolved decision controls this change.
